summary: Built the required double-NAT path: node3 (lan-a, 10.10.1.12) opens TCP connections to node4's HTTP service on port 8080 (lan-b, 10.10.3.13). node1 (VyOS) source-NATs traffic entering the transit network (masquerade to its eth1 address 10.10.2.1) via `nat source rule 100`. node2 (OPNsense) source-NATs traffic entering lan-b via automatic outbound NAT on vtnet2 (masquerade to its lan-b address 10.10.3.254). node4 records the connection as arriving from 10.10.3.254 (node2), never seeing node3's or node1's real address — confirmed via curl and packet captures at every hop (lan-a, transit, lan-b). Interface-to-NIC mapping was discovered empirically via ARP/STP probing since node1 (VyOS, 3 NICs) and node2 (OPNsense, 3 NICs) needed correct pairing with node3/node4's second NICs. Ran the full mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot-identity baselines on all 4 nodes, restarted them one at a time (node1 VyOS reboot, node2 OPNsense shutdown -r, node3/node4 Ubuntu sudo reboot), confirmed changed boot identity on each (boot_id for Linux nodes, kern.boottime for FreeBSD), and re-verified the double-NAT chain end-to-end and per-hop after each restart and after all four restarts completed. All configuration (VyOS config.boot via save, OPNsense config.xml, Ubuntu /etc/network/interfaces.d static configs) persisted correctly across reboots; only the ephemeral test HTTP server on node4 (running from /tmp) needed manual restart after its reboot, which was done and re-verified.
actions_performed: Inspected all 4 nodes' OS/images and NICs (node1=VyOS w/ eth0-2, node2=OPNsense/FreeBSD w/ vtnet0-2, node3/node4=Ubuntu 16.04 w/ ens2+ens7)
Empirically determined interface pairing via ARP/STP capture: node1 eth2<->node3 ens7 (lan-a), node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 (transit), node2 vtnet2<->node4 ens7 (lan-b)

Assigned static IPs: node3 ens7=10.10.1.12/24, node1 eth2=10.10.1.254/24 (lan-a), node1 eth1=10.10.2.1/24, node2 vtnet1(opt1)=10.10.2.2/24 (transit), node2 vtnet2(opt2)=10.10.3.254/24, node4 ens7=10.10.3.13/24 (lan-b)
Configured VyOS node1: nat source rule 100 masquerading eth1 outbound for 10.10.1.0/24, static route 10.10.3.0/24 via 10.10.2.2, committed and saved

Configured OPNsense node2 via config.xml: assigned opt1 (transit/vtnet1) and opt2 (lanb/vtnet2) interfaces, added filter pass rules for both interfaces, verified automatic outbound NAT masquerades traffic egressing vtnet2 to node2's lan-b IP; applied via configctl interface reconfigure and configctl filter reload
Added static route on node3 to 10.10.3.0/24 via 10.10.1.254
Persisted Ubuntu network config via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-ens7.cfg on node3 and node4
Deployed a Python http.server on node4:8080 serving a test page
Verified double-NAT end-to-end via curl and tcpdump captures at lan-a, transit, and lan-b interfaces showing progressive source-address rewriting (10.10.1.12 -> 10.10.2.1 -> 10.10.3.254)
Captured pre-restart boot-identity and health baselines on all 4 nodes
Restarted node1 (VyOS reboot), node2 (OPNsense shutdown -r now), node3 and node4 (Ubuntu sudo reboot) one at a time, polling for command availability after each
Confirmed changed boot identity for each node (boot_id for Linux, kern.boottime for FreeBSD)
Re-verified interface config, NAT/firewall rules, routes, and end-to-end double-NAT connectivity after each individual restart and after all 4 restarts completed
Restarted the ephemeral test HTTP server on node4 after its reboot since it ran from /tmp which was cleared

evidence.requirement: Double NAT path established: node3->node1 (SNAT to transit)->node2 (SNAT to lan-b)->node4, node4 sees source as node2
evidence.summary: Configured VyOS SNAT rule on node1 (masquerade to eth1/10.10.2.1) and confirmed OPNsense automatic outbound NAT on node2 (masquerade to vtnet2/10.10.3.254); packet captures at all three hops (lan-a, transit, lan-b) show progressive source rewriting, with node4 receiving the HTTP GET from 10.10.3.254.

evidence.requirement: Full per-hop packet-level proof of the double translation for the actual HTTP service on port 8080
evidence.summary: Simultaneous tcpdump on node1 eth2 (lan-a, source 10.10.1.12), node1 eth1/node2 vtnet1 (transit, source 10.10.2.1), and node2 vtnet2 (lan-b, source 10.10.3.254) for the same TCP handshake+GET request, proving two independent source rewrites.

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 01e92881...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to e82a3a35... after reboot; interfaces/routes/NAT rule confirmed persisted from config.boot; end-to-end curl through the NAT chain succeeded post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime 06:19:07; reboot acknowledged; boottime changed to 06:30:47 after reboot; opt1/opt2 interface config, filter rules, and NAT persisted from config.xml; end-to-end curl succeeded and tcpdump confirmed source IP still 10.10.3.254 post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node3 (Ubuntu) restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id afd04380...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to ce7bdcbd... after reboot; ens7 static IP and route to lan-b persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d; curl to node4:8080 succeeded post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node4 (Ubuntu) restart baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8660e8f0...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 6883cf31... after reboot; ens7 static IP persisted; HTTP test server (ephemeral, ran from /tmp which was cleared) restarted manually; final tcpdump after all 4 node restarts confirms the double-NAT chain still delivers traffic to node4 with source IP 10.10.3.254.
